faq_heading: Delta market stats: your questions answered

blocks.text: The boards report Delta in 3 parts: Tsawwassen, Ladner and North Delta. In October 2026, Tsawwassen had the highest all-home benchmark at $1,103,800 and Ladner the lowest at $1,023,500, a gap of $80,300. Over twelve months the three-part spread runs Tsawwassen little changed at −1.4%, Ladner down 6.5%, North Delta down 6.8%.
Tsawwassen at a glance, October 2026
Tsawwassen had an all-home benchmark of $1,103,800 (little changed at −1.4% over the year), with detached at $1,469,500, townhouses at $878,400 and apartments at $588,800.
Tsawwassen market stats in full
Ladner at a glance, October 2026
Ladner had an all-home benchmark of $1,023,500 (down 6.5% over the year), with detached at $1,262,500, townhouses at $909,300 and apartments at $620,000.
Ladner market stats in full
North Delta benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical North Delta home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,024,900 in October 2026. That is little changed at +1.3% on the month, down 2.5% over three months, down 4.3% over six months and down 6.8% over the year. Over three years it is down 15.0%, and over five years down 11.8%.
The weakest one-year move in North Delta was for an apartment homes at −11.2%; the strongest was a townhouse at −1.4%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,165,900) and an apartment ($475,700) is $690,200, and a townhouse ($867,500) sits $391,800 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, North Delta is 19.2% above. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 6.8% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, North Delta ranks 1 by all-home benchmark, with South Surrey & White Rock below it at $996,000.

Detached homes in North Delta: benchmark $1,165,900, little changed at +0.6% in a month, down 3.9% in three months, down 6.0% in six months, down 9.2% in a year, down 15.7% in three years and down 13.0% in five. That is 9.9% below the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in North Delta: benchmark $867,500, up 2.6% in a month, up 2.2% in three months, little changed at −1.4% in six months, little changed at −1.4% in a year, down 11.7% in three years and up 1.5% in five. That is 16.9% above the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in North Delta: benchmark $475,700, little changed at −0.7% in a month, down 4.1% in three months, down 7.2% in six months, down 11.2% in a year, down 16.9% in three years and down 2.6% in five. That is 3.2% above the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: Set against October 2025, North Delta had 38 detached sales (31 a year earlier), 3 townhouse sales (3 a year earlier) and 4 apartment sales (8 a year earlier). Month-end active listings were 182 detached (about 267 a year earlier), 32 townhouse (about 31 a year earlier) and 41 apartment (about 53 a year earlier). Dividing sales by active listings gives a sales-to-active ratio of 20.9% for detached, 9.4% for townhouse and 9.8% for apartment.

In dollars, the typical North Delta home is worth about $74,800 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,099,700. By type, detached homes lost about $118,100, from $1,284,000 to $1,165,900, townhouses lost about $12,300, from $879,800 to $867,500, and apartments lost about $60,000, from $535,700 to $475,700 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,071,000 six months ago and near $1,205,800 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $46,100 below the six-month mark and about $180,900 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the North Delta benchmark is about $164,900 above the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $180,900 above.
What the Delta figure is
The $1,103,800 Tsawwassen figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Delta?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Tsawwassen home was $1,103,800, with detached at $1,469,500. In October 2026, a typical Ladner home was $1,023,500, with detached at $1,262,500. In October 2026, a typical North Delta home was $1,024,900, with detached at $1,165,900.

faq.q: Are Delta home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Tsawwassen is little changed at −1.4% over twelve months and little changed at −0.6% over three months. Ladner is down 6.5% over twelve months and down 5.8% over three months. North Delta is down 6.8% over twelve months and down 2.5% over three months.
